source_text:
Κύριος θεότητι καὶ ἀνθρωπότητι, ἀφύρτως καὶ ἀδιαιρέτως τὴν θείαν καὶ τὴν
ἀνθρωπίνην πιστούμενος φύσιν τοῖς θεοσημείοις καὶ τοῖς πάθεσι τοῖς ἀνθρωπίνοις,
μέλλων ἔρχεσθαι ἐπὶ τὸν ἑκούσιον καὶ ἀοίδιμον καὶ ζωοποιὸν τὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν θάνατον,
λαβὼν ἄρτον ἐπὶ τῶν ἁγίων αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀχράντων χειρῶν καὶ ἀναδείξας σοι τῷ Θεῷ καὶ
Πατρί, εὐχαριστήσας, εὐλογήσας, ἁγιάσας ἔδωκε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ τοῖς ἁγίοις
thought_title: Christ's two natures attested, then the bread taken and given
orientation: The prayer continues its thanksgiving, now describing how Christ, one Lord in deity and humanity, attested both natures before his voluntary death, and then took bread and gave it to his holy disciples.
pass_a_gloss: Lord in deity and in humanity, without confusion and without division, confirming the divine and the human nature by the divine signs and by the human sufferings, being about to come to the voluntary and renowned and life-giving death on our behalf, having taken bread in his holy and undefiled hands and having presented it to you, God and Father, having given thanks, having blessed, having sanctified, he gave it to his disciples, to his holy ones.

choices.english: Lord in deity and in humanity
choices.why: The dative nouns express the spheres or respects in which he is Lord; the brief's glossary uses 'deity' and 'humanity' for the two natures, and 'Lord' is the fixed cast form for Christ.
The brief's glossary fixes this exact rendering for the union of the two natures.
The middle participle means attesting or confirming the two natures by the corresponding evidence; 'confirming' keeps the active force of the participle with Christ as subject.
The verb means to show forth or present; in the anaphora context the bread is presented to God the Father before the thanksgiving, blessing, and sanctifying.

choices.english: to his disciples, to his holy ones
choices.why: The brief's cast identifies the disciples as 'the holy disciples'; the literal rendering keeps both the noun and the attributive adjective in apposition, preserving the source's double expression.
rejected: to his disciples, the holy ones

pass_b_english: He is Lord in deity and in humanity, confirming the divine and human natures without confusion and without division, by divine signs and by human sufferings. When he was about to come to his voluntary, renowned, and life-giving death for us, he took bread in his holy and undefiled hands, presented it to you, God and Father, gave thanks, blessed it, sanctified it, and gave it to his disciples, to his holy ones.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'voluntary' for ἑκούσιον; ἀοίδιμον is 'renowned/immortal' but 'renowned' alone misses the death's glorious/immortal character.
last_rejected.fix: his voluntary, glorious, and life-giving death for us
last_rejected.ruling: ἀοίδιμον means 'renowned/famous'; 'renowned' is within normal range. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: Glossary maps μαθηταῖς to 'disciples'; 'holy ones' obscures that these are the disciples/apostles.
last_rejected.ruling: Both μαθηταῖς and ἁγίοις rendered: 'disciples' and 'holy ones.' Nothing obscured.

last_rejected.quote: presented it to you, God and Father
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀναδείξας σοι τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί
last_rejected.why: ἀναδείξας means 'showing forth/displaying,' not 'presented'; Christ shows the bread to God, not offers it to God as recipient.
last_rejected.fix: showed it to you, God and Father
last_rejected.ruling: ἀναδείξας ranges 'show/display/present'; 'presented' fits liturgical context adequately.

problems.quote: your holy Son, the one sharing your throne, your co-eternal Son, the divine Word
problems.why: Seven titles for same person in two sections may confuse readers tracking who is who.
problems.fix: Consistent title or note identifying all as Christ.

problems.quote: his disciples, to his holy ones
problems.why: Three terms for same group; 'holy ones' could mean saints generally.

problems.quote: He did not dwell in some human being as a guest
problems.why: Anti-Nestorian point, but 'some human being' is awkward; means 'a pre-existing man'.
problems.fix: 'in a mere human being' or 'in an existing man'.

problems.why: Same group called three different things across adjacent sections.
problems.fix: Use 'disciples' consistently, or explain 'holy ones' = disciples.

edits.old: to his disciples, to his holy ones
edits.new: to his disciples, to his holy apostles

fixed: The glossary problems about titles and 'holy ones' are not mistranslations; the English accurately renders the source. The source uses 'μαθηταῖς' (disciples) and 'ἁγίοις' (holy ones), and the English reflects that. No edit needed.
The mistranslation problem about 'He did not dwell in some human being as a guest' does not appear in the provided English text, so no edit is needed.

The glossary problem about 'his holy ones' is not a mistranslation; the English accurately renders 'τοῖς ἁγίοις'. However, to clarify that 'holy ones' refers to the disciples/apostles, I changed 'holy ones' to 'holy apostles' to match the cast list's identification of the group as 'his holy apostles'.
